Perhaps the involvement of director Edward Berger could be a benefit here, providing a fresh perspective. After taking over for Doug Liman on The Bourne Supremacy, Paul Greengrass became synonymous with the Jason Bourne franchise, helming the last three entries Damon has starred in. His style proved to be a perfect fit for the series, but a case can be made that the franchise can use some new blood behind the scenes. A different set of eyes coming in and finding a new angle to tackle could revitalize Bourne, and Berger has demonstrated he’s a top-tier filmmaker, directing Best Picture nominees All Quiet on the Western Front and Conclave. He understands the importance of character and could crack an interesting narrative about Jason Bourne himself.
If Berger’s film with Damon falls about, Universal will surely find a way to pivot. Last year, the studio purchased the rights to the Bourne franchise, winning what was described as a “highly competitive” bidding war. Universal would not have shelled out that kind of money to just keep the IP on a shelf collecting dust. More recently, there were reports suggesting Damon’s The Odyssey co-star Zendaya could be in line to take over as the new lead. Granted, Universal has been here before as well. The Bourne Legacy was the first stab at making a Bourne movie sans Damon, and it too had a mixed reception. Of course, that doesn’t mean Zendaya’s reboot is doomed — it just highlights the difficulties of making a new Bourne film that’s worthwhile.

Jason Bourne, whose real name is David Webb, is the protagonist of the spy thriller novel series The Bourne Series, and the most well-known character created by author Robert Ludlum. David Webb was originally a career Force Recon Marine captain and foreign service officer who joined the covert special forces unit "Medusa" during the Vietnam War. He later participated in the highly classified CIA program "Treadstone 71", designed to create an exceptional covert assassin to challenge the renowned terrorist Carlos the Jackal. Webb consequently adopted the new alias "Jason Bourne", a name derived from Jason Charles Bourne, a double agent within "Medusa" during the Vietnam War, whom Webb executed. During a subsequent mission to assassinate Carlos, Bourne unfortunately developed amnesia, forgetting his identity, which marked a turning point in his life. While searching for his identity, Bourne discovered the truth behind his father's death; his father had been killed while attempting to stop the "Treadstone" operation. Ultimately, Bourne regained his true identity but rejected the role of a "killing machine", returning to his name David Webb. The novel series, comprising a total of fifteen books, was written by two authors, Robert Ludlum and Eric Van Lustbader. This includes the original trilogy published by Ludlum between 1980 and 1990, with Van Lustbader taking over the series after Ludlum's death. The novels have been adapted into films and a spin-off television series, with storylines that differ significantly from the books. The role of Jason Bourne has been portrayed by different actors: Richard Chamberlain in the 1988 television film adaptation, and Matt Damon in the newer film series. The latest film, The Bourne Dilemma, is currently in development, with Matt Damon potentially returning to star.

Character Setting

Jason Bourne's real name is David Webb, born on September 13, 1970, in Nixa, State of Missouri. He is a United States Army soldier who served in the Gulf War. Subsequently, he joined the United States Army Special Forces and was promoted to the rank of captain. In The Bourne Ultimatum, his identification card indicates he is a Catholic with blood type B.
1
He is a man without a country, without an identity, without a past. His story begins on the Mediterranean coast of The Republic of Italy—the place where he was found, floating on the sea's surface, unconscious. Later, he learns his name is Jason Bourne and that he has undergone extremely rigorous training, but he cannot recall who turned him into this sophisticated human weapon. Thus, he becomes desperate to uncover his past.
After meeting Marie, Bourne finds himself changing. He is no longer obsessed with searching for his past, although he is often startled awake by fragments of memory. From Marie, he always finds peace. However, Marie is killed by an assassin. Enraged, Bourne embarks on a frenzied quest for revenge because everything he longed for—Marie—is gone forever. He no longer wants to know who he is; he only wishes to forever forget the memories that would surely be unbearable to recall.
Abilities
*   After receiving training, Bourne excelled in various areas including close-quarters combat and the operation of various vehicles.

*   He learned French, German, Spanish, Russian, Italian, and Dutch, making him more formidable than the novel's Bourne, who only spoke French and Southeast Asian dialects.

*   He possesses exceptionally quick reflexes, logical reasoning, crisis detection abilities, keen environmental awareness, and formidable martial arts skills (In *The Bourne Identity*, Bourne fought an assassin who broke into his home using a ballpoint pen; in *The Bourne Supremacy*, Bourne used gas and a toaster along with a magazine to blow up a house; in *The Bourne Ultimatum*, Bourne fought the Blackbriar assassin Desh with a book and a towel).

*   He is also highly proficient in firearms and explosives.

Character Experience
Novel Version
Jason Bourne
Jason Bourne has a long and mysterious past. His real name is David Webb, an American researcher stationed in the Far East specializing in Far Eastern affairs. He married his Thai classmate and had two children, living by the Mekong River in Phnom Penh,
Kingdom of Cambodia
. One day, his wife and children were tragically killed by a bomb dropped from an airplane flying from the north of the river while they were by the Mekong River, in an operation codenamed Delta.
Operation Medusa

Operation Medusa was a high-risk action plan of the U.S. military during the Vietnam War. Its primary missions included assassinating Viet Cong commanders and conducting perilous operations such as infiltrating enemy camps for reconnaissance and sabotage. The operation employed many desperadoes who could receive exceptionally high rewards upon success, which is why it remained highly classified even after the Vietnam War. Operation Medusa was a significant milestone for David Webb; the training he received forged the Bourne who would later confront Carlos. Due to Delta Force (Webb) excelling in various Operation Medusa missions, the Viet Cong issued a bounty and captured Delta Force's brother, Gordon Webb, as a hostage.
Delta began the rescue of his own brother. He formed a team and successfully infiltrated the enemy camp. However, there was a person in the team who had been bribed by the Viet Cong. Delta discovered this in time and brought the double agent back to Tam Quan. This double agent was named Jason Bourne, a Caucasian born in
Commonwealth of Australia
. Delta executed Jason Bourne on March 25, 1968, and Delta also adopted this name to undertake the Treadstone Project.
Treadstone 71
Treadstone 71 was a project under the CIA, located at 71st Street, New York, founded by David Abbott, who held the alias "the Monk." David Webb was recommended by Abbott as the ideal candidate for the Treadstone Project. The primary objective of this project was to lure Carlos, the world's most famous assassin, out of hiding. Webb assumed the identity of a soldier missing in action and independently operated as the assassin "Cain." The Treadstone Project deliberately attributed several assassinations to Cain, building up his reputation. The goal was to diminish Carlos's standing and force him to appear. After three years of executing the Treadstone Project, Cain suddenly lost contact with the operation. Records showed a transfer of funds from his account at the Gemeinschaft Bank in Zurich, leading Treadstone superiors to mistakenly believe Cain had defected. In reality, Cain had been shot, was found floating in the Mediterranean Sea, and was rescued by the captain and crew of a ship. They took him to Dr. Geoffrey Washburn on the nearby island of Port Noir near Marseille for recovery. Although Bourne recovered from his injuries, he suffered from amnesia. The beginning of
The Bourne Series
follows Bourne's journey to reclaim his memories.

Last year, the studio purchased the rights to the Bourne franchise, winning what was described as a “highly competitive” bidding war. Universal would not have shelled out that kind of money to just keep the IP on a shelf collecting dust. More recently, there were reports suggesting Damon’s The Odyssey co-star Zendaya could be in line to take over as the new lead. Granted, Universal has been here before as well. The Bourne Legacy was the first stab at making a Bourne movie sans Damon, and it too had a mixed reception. Of course, that doesn’t mean Zendaya’s reboot is doomed — it just highlights the difficulties of making a new Bourne film that’s worthwhile.

Jason Bourne, whose real name is David Webb, is the protagonist of the spy thriller novel series The Bourne Series, and the most well-known character created by author Robert Ludlum. David Webb was originally a career Force Recon Marine captain and foreign service officer who joined the covert special forces unit "Medusa" during the Vietnam War. He later participated in the highly classified CIA program "Treadstone 71", designed to create an exceptional covert assassin to challenge the renowned terrorist Carlos the Jackal. Webb consequently adopted the new alias "Jason Bourne", a name derived from Jason Charles Bourne, a double agent within "Medusa" during the Vietnam War, whom Webb executed. During a subsequent mission to assassinate Carlos, Bourne unfortunately developed amnesia, forgetting his identity, which marked a turning point in his life. While searching for his identity, Bourne discovered the truth behind his father's death; his father had been killed while attempting to stop the "Treadstone" operation. Ultimately, Bourne regained his true identity but rejected the role of a "killing machine", returning to his name David Webb. The novel series, comprising a total of fifteen books, was written by two authors, Robert Ludlum and Eric Van Lustbader. This includes the original trilogy published by Ludlum between 1980 and 1990, with Van Lustbader taking over the series after Ludlum's death. The novels have been adapted into films and a spin-off television series, with storylines that differ significantly from the books. The role of Jason Bourne has been portrayed by different actors: Richard Chamberlain in the 1988 television film adaptation, and Matt Damon in the newer film series. The latest film, The Bourne Dilemma, is currently in development, with Matt Damon potentially returning to star.

Jason Bourne's real name is David Webb, born on September 13, 1970, in Nixa, State of Missouri. He is a United States Army soldier who served in the Gulf War. Subsequently, he joined the United States Army Special Forces and was promoted to the rank of captain. In The Bourne Ultimatum, his identification card indicates he is a Catholic with blood type B.
1
He is a man without a country, without an identity, without a past. His story begins on the Mediterranean coast of The Republic of Italy—the place where he was found, floating on the sea's surface, unconscious. Later, he learns his name is Jason Bourne and that he has undergone extremely rigorous training, but he cannot recall who turned him into this sophisticated human weapon. Thus, he becomes desperate to uncover his past.
After meeting Marie, Bourne finds himself changing. He is no longer obsessed with searching for his past, although he is often startled awake by fragments of memory. From Marie, he always finds peace. However, Marie is killed by an assassin. Enraged, Bourne embarks on a frenzied quest for revenge because everything he longed for—Marie—is gone forever. He no longer wants to know who he is; he only wishes to forever forget the memories that would surely be unbearable to recall.
Abilities
*   After receiving training, Bourne excelled in various areas including close-quarters combat and the operation of various vehicles.

*   He learned French, German, Spanish, Russian, Italian, and Dutch, making him more formidable than the novel's Bourne, who only spoke French and Southeast Asian dialects.

*   He possesses exceptionally quick reflexes, logical reasoning, crisis detection abilities, keen environmental awareness, and formidable martial arts skills (In *The Bourne Identity*, Bourne fought an assassin who broke into his home using a ballpoint pen; in *The Bourne Supremacy*, Bourne used gas and a toaster along with a magazine to blow up a house; in *The Bourne Ultimatum*, Bourne fought the Blackbriar assassin Desh with a book and a towel).

*   He is also highly proficient in firearms and explosives.

Jason Bourne
Jason Bourne has a long and mysterious past. His real name is David Webb, an American researcher stationed in the Far East specializing in Far Eastern affairs. He married his Thai classmate and had two children, living by the Mekong River in Phnom Penh,
Kingdom of Cambodia
. One day, his wife and children were tragically killed by a bomb dropped from an airplane flying from the north of the river while they were by the Mekong River, in an operation codenamed Delta.
Operation Medusa
texts.3:
Operation Medusa was a high-risk action plan of the U.S. military during the Vietnam War. Its primary missions included assassinating Viet Cong commanders and conducting perilous operations such as infiltrating enemy camps for reconnaissance and sabotage. The operation employed many desperadoes who could receive exceptionally high rewards upon success, which is why it remained highly classified even after the Vietnam War. Operation Medusa was a significant milestone for David Webb; the training he received forged the Bourne who would later confront Carlos. Due to Delta Force (Webb) excelling in various Operation Medusa missions, the Viet Cong issued a bounty and captured Delta Force's brother, Gordon Webb, as a hostage.
Delta began the rescue of his own brother. He formed a team and successfully infiltrated the enemy camp. However, there was a person in the team who had been bribed by the Viet Cong. Delta discovered this in time and brought the double agent back to Tam Quan. This double agent was named Jason Bourne, a Caucasian born in
Commonwealth of Australia
. Delta executed Jason Bourne on March 25, 1968, and Delta also adopted this name to undertake the Treadstone Project.
Treadstone 71
Treadstone 71 was a project under the CIA, located at 71st Street, New York, founded by David Abbott, who held the alias "the Monk." David Webb was recommended by Abbott as the ideal candidate for the Treadstone Project. The primary objective of this project was to lure Carlos, the world's most famous assassin, out of hiding. Webb assumed the identity of a soldier missing in action and independently operated as the assassin "Cain." The Treadstone Project deliberately attributed several assassinations to Cain, building up his reputation. The goal was to diminish Carlos's standing and force him to appear. After three years of executing the Treadstone Project, Cain suddenly lost contact with the operation. Records showed a transfer of funds from his account at the Gemeinschaft Bank in Zurich, leading Treadstone superiors to mistakenly believe Cain had defected. In reality, Cain had been shot, was found floating in the Mediterranean Sea, and was rescued by the captain and crew of a ship. They took him to Dr. Geoffrey Washburn on the nearby island of Port Noir near Marseille for recovery. Although Bourne recovered from his injuries, he suffered from amnesia. The beginning of
The Bourne Series
follows Bourne's journey to reclaim his memories.
